subject.title: [Bug] web_fetch fails in dual-stack networks when DNS returns IPv6 special-use addresses

question: Should OpenClaw relax the default SSRF DNS-answer rule so mixed result sets can proceed after dropping blocked candidates, or keep the current any-blocked-answer fail-closed rule?
rationale: The implementation shape is small, but it changes the default outbound-fetch security boundary and must reflect maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
options.body: Allow the request only when at least one resolved address is allowed, pass only allowed addresses into pinned dispatchers, and add all-blocked plus mixed-answer tests.

options.title: Keep any-blocked fail-closed
options.body: Treat the current behavior as intentional strict SSRF handling and document trusted proxy or fake-IP opt-in paths for affected operators.

options.title: Make mixed DNS explicit opt-in
options.body: Preserve the current default and add or reuse an operator-controlled policy knob for polluted DNS environments.

recommendation.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
recommendation.body: Allow the request only when at least one resolved address is allowed, pass only allowed addresses into pinned dispatchers, and add all-blocked plus mixed-answer tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The central SSRF policy history and current assertion path most directly point to this owner for a security-boundary decision.
